explanation: Allocate a destination array and place the original value at i directly into destination perm[i]. Reading from the unchanged input avoids overwriting values still needed later.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: For each original index i, the assignment writes exactly A[i] to result[perm[i]]. A permutation supplies every destination exactly once, so the result contains every input value at its required destination and no write can destroy an unread input.
walkthrough: With perm=[2,0,1] and values=[10,20,30], place 10 at index 2, 20 at index 0 and 30 at index 1. The result is [20,30,10].
edgeCases: A permutation need not be its own inverse.
An identity permutation leaves the order unchanged.
Equal input values are still moved by their positions.
